messages:
mike_infra: noticed an odd tail-latency skew on a subset of local NVMe hosts in us-west1 during the 02:00-03:00 UTC packer window. GPU packer jobs are getting delayed ~30-90s. :thinking_face:

tara_sre: same - saw a cluster of nodes with 99.9th pct token IO at ~120ms while median is 3ms. impacting gpu backfills.

alex_eng: any commonality? same instance type, same drive firmware?

mike_infra: all A100 nodes w/ wd-nvme-512. firmware v3.1.2. weird thing: device SMART looks normal, wear_pct varies but not extreme. pattern looks time-of-day correlated to janitor scrubs kicking off.

jamie_ops: janitor-bot posted scrub runs at 02:05 on those hosts in us-west1, one and two hour scrubs. maybe overlapping with packer.

janitor-bot: automated scrub job started: scrub-epoch=2026-03-18T02:05Z hosts=[g-node-112, g-node-113, g-node-114] window=2h.

tara_sre: can we throttle janitor or shift window? immediate mitigation would be to reduce scrub concurrency or exclude gpu-backed hosts during packer windows.

mike_infra: quick test: disabled janitor concurrency on one host -> tail latency dropped to baseline in ~10m. looks like scrub IO causing tail spikes.

alex_eng: is this strictly IO saturation or an IO scheduler interaction causing funny tail spikes? can we see iostat + blktrace?

mike_infra: attached quick logs (paste):
```
# iostat -x 1 5
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await svctm %util
nvme0n1 0.00 0.00 12.00 480.00 960.00 38400.00 78.00 0.02 96.20 4.12 98.25 1.10 98.00
```
shows high avgqu-sz during scrub bursts.

tara_sre: that avgqu-sz 0.02 -> 96? ugly. points to bursty metadata IO; scrub may be doing small random reads.

jamie_ops: cost note: if we shift janitor to non-packer window it increases idle window and might delay reclaim; but better than GPU attach failures.

alex_eng: longer term: add io-cgroup for janitor to cap IOPS/bytes, or use blkio throttle per scrub job. Also consider sampling scrub speed to avoid >X iops.

mike_infra: agreed. short term: moving scrub window in us-west1 to 05:00 UTC for next 48h and disabling concurrent scrubs on gpu hosts. I'll patch janitor schedule now.

tara_sre: opened ticket INF-6321 tracking: impact, mitigation, followups (throttle janitor, blkio controls, per-host scrub exclusion, add telemetry for scrub overlap). linking: https://redwood.app/INF-6321

jamie_ops: also flagging possible firmware alignment tech debt: let's collect scrub IO profiles and submit to vendor if pattern repeats.

alex_eng: action items: 1) mike move windows (in flight) 2) tara own INF-6321 3) mike/ops test blkio throttle POC on one canary host 4) follow-up sync tomorrow at 10:00 PST.

mike_infra: done changing schedule, monitoring. will post follow-up if GPU packer latency recovers. :thumbsup:
